Add support bigquery plugin (#26)

* Add BigQuery task shim for v1-to-v2 migration

BigQueryTask is a class-based task in v1 (not a decorator), requiring a
different shimming approach. This adds BigQueryTaskTemplate (a v2

agent/connector automatically.

- New _bigquery.py module with BigQueryTaskTemplate and factory function
- Patches flytekitplugins.bigquery.BigQueryTask at import time
- Creates synthetic flytekitplugins.bigquery module if real plugin is
  not installed (needed on remote containers)
- Fix __init__.py to reference _deck (was _deck_to_report)
- Add flytekitplugins-bigquery to dev dependencies
- Add BigQuery example in examples/bigquery.py
- Add 11 unit tests for the BigQuery shim

Pass _F_SYS_PATH down to child task environments

Stamping the registered spec at deploy time was not enough. A parent workflow
container re-imports the module at runtime and re-serializes its child task
templates from scratch, so the client-side stamp never reached them: the child
action for say_hello_env.say_hello ran at the same version as the registered
spec but with "container env: <NONE>", and still died at
"import flyte_migrate".

The parent's own container does carry the value, because it came from the
registered spec — so child environments now inherit it from os.environ when they
are built. Explicit environment= entries still win.

Give each example its own integration test

Follows the pattern from flyte-sdk's examples/integration_tests.py: one test per
example that imports its entrypoint, so a single example can be re-run from the
IDE and adding one is three lines.

    def test_hello():
        from examples.hello import wf

        _run(wf, "name='flyte'")

The import earns its place — it fails in about a second if the file or the
entrypoint is renamed, or a dependency is missing, instead of after a cluster
round trip. _run reads the file path and function name off the imported object,
so there is no parallel table to keep in sync.

Execution stays in a subprocess. It cannot move in-process: the shim registers
every @workflow into one global parent_env keyed by function name, and six
examples define `wf`, so importing two of them silently overwrites the first —
tests would pass while running the wrong workflow. Importing here is only a name
check; nothing is deployed or run from this process.

Verified: 27 passed in 6m33s with -n 5 against playground.canary.

Add a v1 FlyteFile type transformer

v2's TypeEngine had no transformer for flytekit.types.file.FlyteFile, so it fell
back to pickling the object. That shipped the producing container's local path
and nothing else, and the consumer died with "File /tmp/... does not exist".

The transformer maps FlyteFile to a single-dimension blob, uploading on the way
out and downloading on the way in, both through v2's flyte.io.File. Lookup walks
the MRO, so FlyteFile["csv"] resolves here too and its extension becomes the blob
format.

Two things the obvious implementation gets wrong, both found on the cluster:

- File.from_local can defer the upload; reading .path without running the
  returned lazy_uploader ships a local path.
- A parent workflow serializes a child's inputs on the controller thread, where
  there is no task context to upload from — so a file forwarded from one task to
  another could not be uploaded at all. to_python_value now records the blob URI
  on the downloaded FlyteFile and to_literal reuses it instead of re-uploading.

datatypes_comprehensive now succeeds end to end on the cluster, FlyteFile
round trip included.

Bridge current_context() to the v2 runtime by overriding its properties

_context.py patched ExecutionParameters.__getattr__, which never ran. Python
consults __getattr__ only after normal lookup raises AttributeError, and every
attribute v1 code reads is a real @property on the class -- so the bridge was
dead code for exactly the attributes its own docstring listed.

Nothing raised, either: flytekit's FlyteContextManager.initialize() pre-builds a
local-run safety net (local/local/local ids, local temp paths) so v1 code can run
off-cluster, and the properties returned that. On a v2 cluster the result was a
well-formed, entirely fake value with no error and no warning -- execution_id
collapsing to local:local:local for every run, and raw_output_prefix pointing at
container-local tmp, so offloaded writes succeeded and then vanished with the pod.

Override the properties instead, in three groups:

- backed by v2: execution_id, task_id, raw_output_prefix, logging. execution_id
  maps to ActionID.run_name, not .name -- .name is a single task invocation, so
  using it would hand every task a different id and break the value's main use as
  a run-level correlation key, again silently.
- no v2 source: stats and execution_date warn once, then fall through to v1's
  local value. v1 code usually only logs these; raising would break workflows that
  otherwise run fine.
- left alone: working_directory. v1's contract is a local scratch dir, which the
  fallback already satisfies.

__getattr__ stays, scoped to what it could ever serve -- task-type specific
context, which v1 plugins stash in _attrs under an upper-cased key. Two fixes
there: the None guard missed v2's falsy-but-not-None NULL_TASK_CONTEXT sentinel
and leaked a raw TypeError, and a missing name raised KeyError instead of
AttributeError, which escapes hasattr() and getattr(..., default) and turned v1's
common `if hasattr(ctx, "spark_session")` guard into a crash.

Checkpoint stays unbridged and is marked xfail; v2 has ctx().checkpoints, but
wrapping v1's save/restore/read/write over it is separate work.

Record the local sys.path on environments at deploy time

A v1 LaunchPlan with a schedule becomes a v2 Trigger, and the platform launches
those from the registered spec with no client involved. Those runs all died on
the first line of the module:

    File "/examples/launchplan.py", line 1, in <module>
        import flyte_migrate
    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flyte_migrate'

container env var and the runtime re-adds them before importing the task module.

container had no ./src on its path, and flyte_migrate ships in the code bundle
rather than as an installed package (it is not on PyPI), leaving it unimportable.

flyte.deploy is now wrapped to stamp the same value flyte.run would have. Note
the value has to land on each task template, not just the environment: the
container env is serialized from task_template.env_vars, which was copied off
the environment back when the task was decorated.

Keep _task annotations lazy so the shim imports on older flytekit

_task.py annotates three signatures with Union[bool, flytekit.Cache].
Module-level annotations are evaluated eagerly, and flytekit.Cache only
exists in newer flytekit, so importing flyte_migrate inside a v1 image
built against an older flytekit dies before any user code runs:

  File ".../flyte_migrate/_task.py", line 38, in <module>
      def _translate_cache_policy(cache: Union[bool, flytekit.Cache]) -> ...
  AttributeError: module 'flytekit' has no attribute 'Cache'

Hit by the upgrade flow, which pip-installs the shim into the user's own
image (deck example, run ubcskm4bh2c7l6rslnsh). Cache is referenced only
in annotations and never at runtime, so `from __future__ import
annotations` is enough — and unlike pinning a flytekit floor it does not
force an upgrade of flytekit inside images we do not control.
